draw.method: random.sample over 1-based source lines of project/dataset.jsonl

rows.note: A date picker refusing 29 February is a real defect with an obvious workaround, which is what SEV3 names on this ladder.
A stretched empty-state illustration on wide monitors is presentational only, and Low is the bottom class of this ticket system's vocabulary.

A checklist ticking a step that has not been done is a correctness defect shown to the user, and SEV4 is the bottom class; the only ladder this scenario ships is the one inside agent.py's `rubric` prompt style -- SEV3 limited impact with a workaround, SEV4 cosmetic -- and a prompt the optimizer tunes over is not a statement of how the labels were decided, so there is no published rule to adjudicate this against. On that ladder SEV3 fits at least as well.
One integration's retry storm starving every other queue degrades service for unrelated tenants, which is the major-degradation class SEV2.
A partner rejected by our idempotency window because their clock runs eight minutes fast is a live integration failure for that partner, so P2 on this system's scale is sensible.
